chart_references: The last few years have been far bubblier for Coca-Cola, whose market value has risen by 23% since the start of 2023, than for Pepsi, which has slumped by 15% (see chart). Pepsi’s troubles stem in part from the hefty price rises it applied to its food and beverages amid the post-pandemic surge in inflation, exceeding even those of its competitors. That strategy has lately backfired as cost-conscious shoppers have fled to upstart brands and retailers’ in-house alternatives.

extraction.title: Soda wars
extraction.subtitle: Coca-Cola is trouncing Pepsi. Can the underdog turn things around? The maker of the world’s second-favourite fizzy drink is becoming more like its rival
extraction.summary: Coca-Cola leads the soft-drink market with a 17% share, while Pepsi holds 11%. Pepsi's recent struggles stem from price increases and changing consumer preferences. An activist investor's involvement has prompted Pepsi to cut costs and streamline its product range, showing early signs of recovery.
